records.issue_text: [High/bug] CalendarService.ts (google):315-317 — In `deleteEvent`, falsy `externalCalendarId` causes comparison against null/undefined id, never matches, and yields `calendarId: undefined`, producing a malformed request (`/calendars/undefined/events`); old code fell back to destination calendar's externalId
records.rationale: The diff changes deleteEvent to `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When externalCalendarId is falsy, the fallback searches for a calendar whose externalId equals the falsy value (undefined/null/empty), which never matches, so calendarId becomes undefined instead of the old behavior of falling back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Same pattern in updateEvent. This produces a malformed calendar deletion/update request — a real defect introduced by this diff.

records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] CalendarService.ts (google):145-149 — When credential's destination calendar isn't found, `createEvent` silently falls back to `"primary"`, booking the event on the wrong calendar instead of erroring
records.rationale: The diff explicitly shows `const selectedCalendar = calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId;` and then `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. Since EventManager now invokes createEvent once per destination calendar with the credential's id, a mismatch (destination without matching credentialId) silently books to the default 'primary' calendar instead of surfacing an error. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff; whether it's intended fallback behavior is uncertain, so confidence is moderate.

records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] handleNewBooking.ts:1098 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently does nothing when `destinationCalendar` is null, dropping team members' destination calendars instead of initializing the array
records.rationale: The diff sets `destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar] : null`, then calls `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` only when isTeamEventType && COLLECTIVE. When the ternary yields null, optional chaining makes push a no-op, so team members' destination calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are silently dropped rather than the array being initialized — a real correctness gap in the newly added code.

records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] EventManager.ts & handleCancelBooking.ts — `prisma.credential.findUnique` runs sequentially inside a per-reference/destination loop with duplicated logic; N destinations cause N sequential round-trips that could be batched
records.rationale: The diff genuinely adds `prisma.credential.findUnique` inside per-destination/per-reference loops (EventManager.ts createAllCalendarEvents and updateAllCalendarEvents, and handleCancelBooking.ts), each wrapped in sequential `for...of` loops with duplicated credential-fetch logic. This is a true, specific observation of N sequential DB round-trips that could be batched, decision-relevant for a maintainer (latency under multi-destination collective bookings), and not a correctness bug or style nit.
